(Currently Amended) Claim 1: A method, comprising: transmitting a sequence of light pulses having a first speed; receiving a second sequence of light pulses from a vehicle; and transmitting a message as a sequence of light pulses having a second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the first speed is different from the second speed, and wherein the method does not encompass transitory signals.

(Currently Amended) Claim 2: The method of claim 1, wherein a computing device determines the second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle that is slower than the first speed, and wherein the method does not encompass transitory signals.

(Currently Amended) Claim 3: The method of claim 2, wherein the computing device determines when the vehicle is no longer in proximity and transmits a sequence of light pulses having a third speed, wherein the third speed is faster than the second speed, and wherein the method does not encompass transitory signals.

(Currently Amended) Claim 4: The method of claim 3, wherein the computing device receives a third sequence of light pulses from a third vehicle and transmits the message as a sequence of light pulses having a third speed based on the third sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the third speed is different from the second speed, and wherein the method does not encompass transitory signals.

(Currently Amended) Claim 6: The method of claim 1, wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status, encoded into light pulses as binary bits, wherein the encoding is independent of message transmission speed, and wherein the method does not encompass transitory signals.

(Currently Amended) Claim 11: An apparatus, comprising: a processor; a memory, the memory storing instructions executable by the processor to: transmit a sequence of light pulses having a first speed; receive a second sequence of light pulses from a vehicle; and transmit a message as a sequence of light pulses having a second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the first speed is different from the second speed, and wherein the apparatus does not encompass transitory signals.

(Currently Amended) Claim 12: The apparatus of claim 11, wherein a computing device determines the second speed based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle that is slower than the first speed, and wherein the apparatus does not encompass transitory signals.

(Currently Amended) Claim 13: The apparatus of claim 12, wherein the computing device determines when the vehicle is no longer in proximity and transmits a sequence of light pulses having a third speed, wherein the third speed is faster than the second speed, and wherein the apparatus does not encompass transitory signals.

(Currently Amended) Claim 14: The apparatus of claim 13, wherein the computing device receives a third sequence of light pulses from a third vehicle and transmits the message as a sequence of light pulses having a third speed based on the third sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the third speed is different from the second speed, and wherein the apparatus does not encompass transitory signals.

(Currently Amended) Claim 16: The apparatus of claim 11, wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status, encoded into light pulses as binary bits, wherein the encoding is independent of message transmission speed, and wherein the apparatus does not encompass transitory signals.
